newsitem.title: INDIA: Airgas subsidiary buys stake in India firm.
newsitem.headline: Airgas subsidiary buys stake in India firm.

text.p: A subsidiary of U.S. firm Airgas Inc. has acquired a 25 percent stake in India's Superior Air Products, an official at the Indian company said on Saturday.
"Airgas is keen to come into the Indian market and has taken financial participation in our company," Sanjeev Kaul, deputy company secretary at Superior, told Reuters.

Mauritius Industrial Gases Inc, (MIGI) a wholly owned subsididary of Airgas Inc., has been alloted 950,000 10-rupee face value shares at a price of 101 rupees each, the company said in a statement to the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE).
Superior Air stock closed at 19.60 rupees on Friday at the BSE in volume of 2,700 shares.

The statement said the firm also issued 364,500 warrants of 52 rupees each to the promoters, their business associates and to MIGI. Each warrant is convertible into one 10-rupee face value equity stock.
"When the whole process is over in phases, Airgas would hold about 25.5 percent of our equity," Kaul said.
Superior Air Products is a manufacturer of basic industrial gases and supplies to the iron and steel industry, medical hospitals and ordinance factories.
The company reported sales of 1.5 million rupees in the year to March 31, 1996.
